newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW says 1996 results hit by pension change. [CORRECTED 17:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: VW says 1996 results hit by pension change. [CORRECTED 17:50 GMT]

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG said on Thursday that its 1996 group profit of 678 million marks, a near doubling from 1995 (corrects year from 1996), was burdened by a change in its provisions for pension requirements.
VW said in its annual report that the interest rate used for determining the pensions has been lowered to five percent from six percent at a cost of about 1.5 billion marks.

"In order to establish more effective provisions for the future financial burden arising from pension payments, an interest rate of five percent, in contrast to the principle applied in the financial statements of Volkswagen AG, has been applied as of January 1, 1996," VW said in its annual report.
"This adjustment reduces profit by 1.489 million marks," the carmaker said.
VW chief financial officer Bruno Adelt said in the text of a speech at the carmaker's annual news conference that the change was due to currently lower German interest rates.
